name: History trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about world and US history, from ancient times to about 2000. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: The oldest surviving peace treaty, concluded around 1259 BCE, was agreed between Pharaoh Ramesses II and which Hittite king?
items.explain: The Egyptian–Hittite treaty was concluded between Ramesses II and Hattusili III. Muwatalli II was the Hittite king at the earlier Battle of Kadesh.

items.question: Which archaeologist found the Cyrus Cylinder at Babylon in 1879 while excavating for the British Museum?
items.explain: The Assyro-British archaeologist Hormuzd Rassam discovered the Cyrus Cylinder in March 1879 during a British Museum excavation programme in Mesopotamia.

items.question: In 405 BCE, which naval battle in the Hellespont saw Lysander's Spartan fleet destroy the Athenian navy and effectively end the Peloponnesian War?
items.explain: At Aegospotami, Lysander surprised the beached Athenian fleet and captured almost all of it. Athens surrendered the following spring.

items.question: Which pair of consuls led the large Roman army that Hannibal crushed at Cannae in 216 BCE?
items.explain: The Romans at Cannae were led by the consuls Lucius Aemilius Paullus and Gaius Terentius Varro.

items.question: Which eastern co-emperor joined Constantine in issuing the 313 Edict of Milan, which ended the persecution of Christians?
items.explain: The edict was issued in the names of Constantine, who ruled the West, and Licinius, who ruled the East. They had met in Milan for the wedding of Licinius to Constantine's sister.

items.question: Who commanded Octavian's fleet at the Battle of Actium in 31 BCE?
items.explain: Octavian's fleet at Actium was commanded by his close friend and general Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, who defeated the fleets of Antony and Cleopatra.

items.question: Remorse over the bloody conquest of which region led the Mauryan emperor Ashoka to renounce armed conquest and embrace Buddhism?
items.explain: Ashoka conquered Kalinga (modern Odisha) in the eighth year of his reign. The suffering the war caused moved him to renounce armed conquest.

items.question: Which Seljuk sultan defeated and captured the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV Diogenes at Manzikert in 1071?
items.explain: Alp Arslan's Seljuk Turks defeated the Byzantine army at Manzikert on 26 August 1071. He captured the emperor and released him only after he agreed to cede territory.

items.question: Which pope nullified Magna Carta only about ten weeks after King John sealed it in 1215?
items.explain: The U.S. National Archives notes that Pope Innocent III annulled the agreement about ten weeks after John sealed it, and England fell into civil war.

items.question: The 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas set its dividing meridian 370 leagues west of which island group?
items.explain: The treaty moved the papal line to a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. This put Brazil on the Portuguese side.

items.question: Which 1529 treaty divided the other side of the world between Spain and Portugal by fixing the antimeridian of the Tordesillas line?
items.explain: The Treaty of Zaragoza, signed on 22 April 1529, specified the antimeridian to the Tordesillas line, dividing the Pacific side of the world.

items.question: Which Mamluk sultan's realm did Mansa Musa of Mali pass through on his famous 1324 pilgrimage, when his spending in Cairo depressed gold's value?
items.explain: Al-Umari's account describes Musa's reception on behalf of the sultan al-Malik al-Nasir, and says Musa's gold lowered gold's price in Egypt.

source.title: Al-Umari's Account of Mansa Musa's Visit to Cairo

items.question: Which Umayyad governor of al-Andalus was killed leading the army defeated by Charles Martel at the Battle of Tours in 732?
items.explain: Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, governor of al-Andalus, led the Umayyad force and was killed at Tours on 10 October 732.

items.question: Which cannon-founder, who left Constantinople and offered his services to Mehmed II, cast the giant bombard used in the 1453 siege?
items.explain: Orban (Urban) approached Mehmed II after leaving Constantinople, and he cast the great bombard that helped breach the city's walls.

items.question: In the negotiations that produced the 1648 Peace of Westphalia, which city hosted the talks involving Sweden?
items.explain: The Osnabrück treaty was drafted between the Holy Roman Empire and Sweden. The empire's agreement with France was drafted in Münster.

items.question: The 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk between Russia and Qing China followed Russia's defeat at the siege of which Amur fortress?
items.explain: The treaty followed Russia's defeat at the Siege of Albazin. It left the Amur region to the Qing.

items.question: How many original copies of the 1215 Magna Carta are known to survive today?
items.explain: Britannica notes that four original copies of the 1215 Magna Carta survive.

items.question: After the Roman disaster at Carrhae in 53 BCE, which Parthian king had his victorious general Surena put to death?
items.explain: Surena, who beat Crassus at Carrhae, was killed by his own king, Orodes II, because his achievements had made him too dangerous.

items.question: The Roman army of Crassus was destroyed in 53 BCE near the ancient town of Carrhae, known today by what name?
items.explain: Carrhae is the ancient name of Harran, in present-day Turkey, near where Crassus met the Parthians.

items.question: Arminius, who destroyed three Roman legions in AD 9, was a chieftain of which Germanic tribe?
items.explain: Arminius was a Roman-trained chieftain of the Cherusci, and he led the ambush that defeated Varus in the Teutoburg Forest.

items.question: Which three legions were lost with Varus in the Teutoburg Forest in AD 9?
items.explain: Varus was leading the XVII, XVIII and XIX legions to winter quarters when Arminius ambushed them.

source.title: The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest and the founding myth of the German nation

items.question: Which countess, a leading Italian supporter of Pope Gregory VII, inherited Canossa Castle, where Henry IV did penance in 1077?
items.explain: Matilda of Tuscany inherited Canossa in 1052 and invited Gregory VII to take refuge there during his dispute with Henry IV.

items.question: Although Henry IV was absolved at Canossa, which man did German nobles elect as antiking in March 1077?
items.explain: Nobles opposed to Henry IV elected Rudolf of Rheinfelden, Duke of Swabia, as antiking in March 1077, even though Henry had been absolved.

items.question: In 1202 the Fourth Crusade's army helped Venice retake which rebellious Dalmatian port city as payment for its transport?
items.explain: Doge Enrico Dandolo proposed that the Crusaders attack the rebellious city of Zara (Zadar) instead of paying Venice in cash.

items.question: Who was chosen in May 1204 as the first Latin Emperor of Constantinople after the city fell to the Fourth Crusade?
items.explain: Count Baldwin of Flanders was made the first Latin Emperor of Constantinople on 9 May 1204, a few weeks after the sack.

items.question: At Panipat in 1526, which flanking tactic did Babur use to surround Ibrahim Lodi's much larger army?
items.explain: Babur split his army into left, right and centre units with flanking forces, a method called tulughma, which let his smaller force encircle the Lodi army.

items.question: Babur's victory at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 ended the rule of which Delhi Sultanate dynasty?
items.explain: Ibrahim Lodi, the last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, was killed at Panipat, which opened the way for Mughal rule in India.

items.question: Which pope arranged the Holy League coalition whose fleet defeated the Ottomans at Lepanto in 1571?
items.explain: The Holy League was a coalition of Catholic states arranged by Pope Pius V, with the Spanish and Venetian navies leading its fleet.

items.question: Which Habsburg negotiated the 1555 Peace of Augsburg on behalf of Emperor Charles V, his brother?
items.explain: Ferdinand, King of the Romans, acted for Charles V at the Diet of Augsburg and pushed through the agreement that included cuius regio, eius religio.

items.question: Under the 1555 Peace of Augsburg's 'ecclesiastical reservation', what happened to a Catholic prince-bishop who converted to Lutheranism?
answers: He could keep his lands and convert his subjects
He kept his lands but a regent had to rule them
He had to give up his rule, so the lands stayed Catholic
He could secularize his lands as a hereditary duchy
items.correct: He had to give up his rule, so the lands stayed Catholic
items.explain: The ecclesiastical reservation required church rulers who changed religion to give up their rule, which kept their territories Catholic.

items.question: Which ruler issued the Edict of Potsdam in late October 1685, encouraging Huguenots expelled from France to settle in his lands?
items.explain: Right after Louis XIV's Edict of Fontainebleau, Frederick William of Brandenburg issued the Edict of Potsdam to welcome Protestant refugees.

items.question: Louis XIV's 1685 Edict of Fontainebleau revoked an edict that had been signed in 1598 by which French king?
items.explain: Henry IV signed the Edict of Nantes in 1598, giving Huguenots substantial rights. His grandson Louis XIV revoked it in 1685.

items.question: Which commander of Siraj ud-Daulah's army betrayed him at Plassey in 1757 and succeeded him as Nawab of Bengal?
items.explain: Mir Jafar secretly sided with Robert Clive and the East India Company, and he was installed as Nawab after Siraj ud-Daulah's defeat.

items.question: In Marbury v. Madison (1803), the Supreme Court found part of which law to be unconstitutional?
items.explain: Chief Justice John Marshall ruled that the provision of the Judiciary Act of 1789 giving the Court the power to issue Marbury's writ was unconstitutional.

items.question: William Marbury, whose undelivered commission started the famous 1803 case, had been appointed to what office by outgoing President John Adams?
answers: Collector of the Port of Baltimore
Marshal of the District of Columbia
Justice of the peace in the District of Columbia
items.correct: Justice of the peace in the District of Columbia
items.explain: In 1801 Adams issued Marbury a commission as a justice of the peace, but the new Secretary of State, James Madison, refused to deliver it.

items.question: Which statesman chaired the Congress of Vienna, held from September 1814 to June 1815?
items.explain: Austria's Klemens von Metternich chaired the Congress, which reorganized Europe after the Napoleonic Wars.

items.question: In January 1815, Talleyrand signed a secret defensive alliance at the Congress of Vienna joining France with which two powers?
items.explain: The Secret Treaty of Vienna of 3 January 1815 was signed by France, Austria and Great Britain, which ended France's diplomatic isolation.

items.question: Which Illinois senator offered the amendment that banned slavery in the rest of the Louisiana Purchase north of 36°30′ in the Missouri Compromise?
items.explain: Senator Jesse B. Thomas of Illinois proposed the compromise amendment that admitted Missouri as a slave state and barred slavery above 36°30′.

items.question: Maine entered the Union as a free state in 1820 after separating from which existing state?
items.explain: Maine had been part of Massachusetts, and its separation and admission as a free state was paired with Missouri's admission as a slave state.

items.question: Which Mexican president signed the December 1853 treaty that sold the Mesilla Valley region to the United States in the Gadsden Purchase?
items.explain: Santa Anna's government, in financial distress, agreed to the sale negotiated with US minister James Gadsden.

items.question: Before becoming US minister to Mexico, James Gadsden headed which railroad company and wanted a southern transcontinental route?
items.explain: Gadsden was president of the South Carolina Railroad Company and believed the best transcontinental route ran through part of northern Mexico.

items.question: The 1842 Treaty of Nanking ending the First Opium War was signed aboard which British warship?
items.explain: The treaty was signed on 29 August 1842 aboard HMS Cornwallis at Nanjing, then called Nanking.

source.title: Treaty of Nanking - New World Encyclopedia

items.question: Which British diplomat replaced Charles Elliot and pressed the harsher demands that led to the Treaty of Nanking?
items.explain: Palmerston dismissed Elliot for not extracting enough concessions, and his replacement Pottinger demanded compensation and more open ports.

items.question: Which city did the Taiping rebels capture in 1853 and rename Tianjing, making it their capital?
items.explain: The Taipings took Nanjing in 1853 and ran their Heavenly Kingdom from it until Qing forces recaptured it in 1864.

items.question: Hong Xiuquan, leader of the Taiping Rebellion, belonged to which ethnic group?
items.explain: Hong Xiuquan was an ethnic Hakka who proclaimed himself the younger brother of Jesus Christ after a series of visions.

items.question: Which document, linked to Pope Gregory VII's push to reform lay investiture, met resistance from Emperor Henry IV?
items.explain: Gregory VII's reforms of investiture, set out in the Dictatus papae, were resisted by Henry IV, leading to the Walk to Canossa.

items.question: Which Venetian commander defended Famagusta for about eleven months before asking for a truce and surrendering in 1571?
items.explain: Marco Antonio Bragadin commanded the besieged Venetian garrison at Famagusta in Cyprus until he sought a truce and surrendered in the summer of 1571.

items.question: Which Byzantine prince persuaded Boniface of Montferrat and the Venetians to divert the Fourth Crusade to Constantinople to restore his father Isaac II?
items.explain: Alexios IV Angelos, son of the deposed Isaac II, persuaded the Crusader leaders to divert to Constantinople to reinstate his father as co-emperor.

items.question: Which of these cities was NOT among the five treaty ports opened to British trade by the 1842 Treaty of Nanking?
items.explain: The Treaty of Nanking opened Canton, Amoy, Foochow, Shanghai and Ningpo. Tientsin was opened later, by the 1860 Convention of Peking, which followed the 1858 Treaty of Tientsin.

items.question: At the Congress of Vienna, Talleyrand urged Austria and Britain to secretly block Prussia from annexing all of which German kingdom?
items.explain: Talleyrand divided the Allies by backing secret agreements to stop Russia annexing all of Poland and Prussia annexing all of Saxony.

source.title: Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand, prince de Bénévent - Diplomat, Statesman, France
